title: 第4章 鲤跃龙门
novel_title: 御兽仙朝：我能设计进化形态
content_zh:
天刚亮。

    稻花村村口的老槐树下已经聚集了很多人。

    赵老六来得最早，扛着锄头，本来是要去地里的，瞅见罗家那边有动静，锄头往墙根一靠，就过来了。

    张婶也来了，怀里的洗衣狐的尾巴已经耷拉下来，大清早还没有睡醒的样子。

    刘瘸子拿着拐杖，在人群中站在后面，脖子伸得很长。

    还有一些平时和罗家不太来往的人，也都三三两两地聚过来了。

    嘴上说着“路过看看”，脚底下却站得纹丝不动。

    乡下这样的情况，哪家有什么大事小情不用通知，消息自己长了腿，一夜之间全村都知道了。

    罗影站在村口的土路上，身上穿的还是那件灰扑扑的短褐，不过浆洗过了，补丁上的线脚也重新收了一遍。

    书箱背在身后，里面装着几件换洗衣裳，一包李子诚昨天留下的饼，还有用旧布裹了三层的牛角。

    六两银子的分量，隔着布都能感觉到那股子沉。

    他身后，罗川推着一辆破旧的独轮车。

    车上半靠半坐着罗长庚，腰上的绷带换了新的，旱烟杆子别在腰间，没点。

    罗长庚脸色不好，昨晚一夜没睡，眼窝子塌下去一圈，颧骨上的皮紧绷绷的。

    但他把脊背挺得笔直。

    送儿子上县学，他得撑住这个面子。

    赵老六走到跟前，搓了搓自己的手，然后笑了一下。

    “影子今天就要走了”

    “嗯，赵叔。”

    “好事，好事。”

    赵老六点着头，眼睛在罗影身上转了一圈，又看了看罗长庚，嘴张了张，想问什么，到底没问出口。

    他想问的问题，在场的人都想问。

    罗家哪里来的六两银子？

    上几周，整个村庄都知道，罗家连县学的门槛都够不着。

    罗长庚躺在床上愁得一根接一根抽旱烟...

    罗川白天种地晚上还琢磨去码头扛货。

    怎么就一晚上凑足了？

    可没人说。

    乡下人的规矩，在送人上路的时候不说丧气话，也不问窝心事。

    张婶倒是慷慨，挤到前面来，从怀里掏出一个粗布小包，硬塞到罗影手里。

    “婶子煮的茶叶蛋，路上垫垫。到了县城别省着吃，读书费脑子。”

    罗影接过之后，握了握它，蛋壳有些粗糙，有些温润：

    “感谢张婶。”

    张婶摆了摆手，又回到了人群之中。

    嘴里嘟囔着一句话，声音很低，听不清楚，但是眼圈已经有些发红了。

    稻花村上一次有学生到县学读书的人，是六年前刘家老三的儿子。

    刘老三家底比罗家厚些，他早年做过牛贩子，攒了点家底，供他的娃读了县学。

    后来没通过考核就回来了，在他爹老三的带领下，在镇上开起了一个小杂货铺。

    比起种地的生活来，还要强一些...

    但也就这样了。

    六年。

    一个村子，六年才出一个读书人。

    这就是乡下。

    村子口停放着一匹叫做【追风驹】的良驹。

    个子不算大，比普通的马矮了差不多一个小头。

    毛色是红色和黑色混合而成，四条腿很细长，一条条的肌肉都绷了起来，就像琴弦一样。

    它站在这里也不老实，前蹄刨着地面，鼻孔张翕着，像是随时要撒开蹄子跑出去。

    这是镇上脚行的马匹。

    往县城跑一趟，得花两百文。

    两百文是什么概念？

    罗川在地里刨了大约一个月的时间，除去吃穿喝用这些日常开销之后，就只剩下了这些。

    但钱不能不花。

    揣着六两银子做的牛角，在稻花村到县城的路上，人走路要两个多时辰。

    这一路上，荒段不少。

    若是太平年景倒还好，可今年入秋以来，邻县闹过一回兽灾。

    几只野化的【裂牙狼】从山里蹿出来，虽说后来被巡兽使带队清了，但零星的散狼没抓干净，隔三差五还有人在山道上撞见。

    寻常商户走远路，讲究的会雇一只【铁脊豺】做护卫。

    那东西体型跟半大的驴差不多，皮粗肉厚，脊背上一排铁灰色的硬鬃竖着，跟钢针似的，凶起来连野狼都不敢近身。

    再讲究些的，还会带一只【瞭远猴】打头阵。

    猴子眼神好，蹲在高处能望出去三四里地，有什么风吹草动提前叫唤，主人好做准备。

    但那是有钱人的排场。

    一只【铁脊豺】跑一趟县城要八百文，加上【瞭远猴】就是一两二。

    罗家花不起。

    【追风驹】是穷人的选择。

    它不能打，遇上野兽也就只有跑的份。

    但它跑得快。

    觉醒2级的【追风驹】有一门天生技能叫【拂风】，能借着风向加速，顺风的时候跑起来比寻常马快出两倍不止。

    若是真碰上了危险，它还能短时间内爆发一次【快冲】技能，四蹄翻飞，风裹着土烟，一眨眼就蹿出去百丈远。

    跑不过它的东西，追不上。

    追得上它的东西，这一片乡下也碰不着。

    两刻钟到县城。

    快进快出，不给路上留空档。

    穷人的安全，就靠一个快字。

    罗长庚让罗川把独轮车推到【追风驹】跟前，撑着车沿慢慢站了起来。

    他腰不好，站起来的动作很慢，整个人弓着，像一把被压弯了的旧弓。

    他抬起头，看着那匹【追风驹】。

    【追风驹】歪着脑袋看了他一眼，鼻子喷了一口气，不耐烦地刨了两下蹄子。

    罗长庚没有像对人一样打招呼。

    他是对着这匹马，认认真真地弯了一下腰。

    弯得很深，腰伤扯得他龇了一下牙，但没吭声。

    “劳驾了。我家小子头一回去县城，路上......麻烦照应着些。”

    他从怀里摸出一个布包，打开，里面是一串铜钱，数过的，整整两百文，拿麻绳穿着，一枚不多一枚不少。

    他把铜钱轻轻放在追风驹鞍侧的褡裢口袋上。

    【追风驹】低头看了看那串铜钱，又看了看罗长庚，打了一个响鼻。

    算是应了。

    脚行的老赵在一旁叼着草根看了这一幕，没说什么，只是把【追风驹】的缰绳紧了紧，朝罗影努了努嘴。

    “上来吧，小子。抓稳了，这畜生脾气急，起步的时候颠。”

    罗影翻身上了马背。

    【追风驹】的背脊比老黑窄得多，也硬得多，硌着屁股骨生疼。

    他一只手抓着缰绳，另一只手按了按身侧书箱里那个裹着三层旧布的牛角，确认还在。

    然后他回过头。

    罗长庚站在独轮车旁边，一只手扶着车把，另一只手垂在身侧，旱烟杆子别在腰间，风吹着他花白的鬓角。

    罗川站在他爹身后，两只手插在腰带里，嘴抿得紧紧的，眼眶红着，但没说话。

    再后面是赵老六、张婶、刘瘸子，还有几个叫不上名字的乡亲。

    都站着。

    都看着他。

    罗影张了张嘴，想说点什么。

    可话到嘴边，又觉得什么都不对。
content_en:
It's just dawn.
Many people have gathered under the old locust tree at the entrance of Daohua Village.
Zhao Laoliu was the first to arrive, carrying a hoe. He was originally going to the fields. When he saw movement from the Luo family, he leaned the hoe against the wall and came over.
Aunt Zhang also came. The tail of the laundry fox in her arms had drooped down, and she didn't seem to wake up yet in the early morning.
Liu Laizi was holding a cane and standing in the back of the crowd, his neck stretched out.
There were also some people who didn't usually have much contact with the Luo family, but they also gathered in twos and threes.
He said "pass by and take a look", but he stood motionless under his feet.
In a situation like this in the countryside, no family needs to be notified of any big or small incident. The news spreads on its own, and the whole village knows about it overnight.
Luo Ying stood on the dirt road at the entrance of the village. He was still wearing the dusty brown shorts, but they had been starched and the stitching on the patches had been tightened again.
The bookcase was carried behind his back, containing a few changes of clothes, a pack of cakes left by Li Zicheng yesterday, and an ox horn wrapped three times in old cloth.
The weight of six taels of silver can be felt through the cloth.
Behind him, Luo Chuan pushed a dilapidated wheelbarrow.
Luo Changgeng was half-reclining and half-sitting in the car. The bandage on his waist was replaced with a new one, and the dry tobacco pole was pinned to his waist, unlit.
Luo Changgeng looked bad. He didn't sleep last night. His eye sockets were sunken and the skin on his cheekbones was tight.
But he straightened his back.
He had to keep up the honor of sending his son to the county school.
Zhao Laoliu walked up to him, rubbed his hands, and then smiled.
"Shadow is leaving today"
"Yes, Uncle Zhao."
"Good thing, good thing."
Zhao Laoliu nodded, his eyes turned around Luo Ying, then looked at Luo Changgeng, and opened his mouth, wanting to ask something, but he didn't ask.
He wanted to ask questions that everyone present wanted to ask.
Where did the Luo family get six taels of silver?
In the past few weeks, the entire village knew that the Luo family could not even reach the threshold of the county school.
Luo Changgeng lay on the bed and smoked cigarettes one after another...
Luo Chuan farmed during the day and thought about going to the dock to carry goods at night.
How come you got it all in one night?
But no one said anything.
The rule of country people is not to say anything depressing or ask anyone's concerns when sending someone off.
Aunt Zhang was generous and squeezed to the front, took out a small coarse cloth bag from her arms and forced it into Luo Ying's hand.
"The tea eggs cooked by my aunt are used as cushions on the road. Don't skimp on food when you get to the county town. Reading is a waste of time."
After Luo Ying took it, he shook it. The eggshell was a little rough and a little warm:
"Thank you Aunt Zhang."
Aunt Zhang waved her hand and returned to the crowd.
He muttered something in his mouth, his voice was very low and could not be heard clearly, but his eye circles were already a little red.
The last time a student from Daohua Village came to the county school to study was the son of the third son of the Liu family six years ago.
Liu Laosan's family is richer than the Luo family. He worked as a cattle dealer in his early years and saved some money for his children to attend the county school.
Later, he came back after failing the examination. Under the leadership of his father, he opened a small grocery store in the town.
It's better than farming life...
But that’s about it.
Six years.
In a village, it takes only six years for a scholar to appear.
This is the countryside.
Parked at the entrance of the village is a good horse called "Chasing the Wind Horse".
He is not very big, almost a head shorter than an ordinary horse.
The fur color is a mixture of red and black, the four legs are very slender, and the muscles are all stretched out, like piano strings.
It was not honest standing here, with its front hooves digging at the ground and its nostrils flaring, as if it was about to spread its hooves and run out at any moment.
These are the horses walking around town.
A trip to the county seat costs two hundred coins.
What is the concept of two hundred articles?
Luo Chuan dug in the fields for about a month, and after excluding daily expenses such as food, clothing and drink, this was all he had left.
But money cannot be spent.
Carrying an ox horn made of six taels of silver, it takes more than two hours to walk from Daohua Village to the county seat.
There are many deserted sections along the way.
It would be fine in a peaceful year, but since autumn this year, there has been an animal disaster in the neighboring county.
Several feral [Split-Tooth Wolves] jumped out of the mountains. Although they were later cleared by the patrolling team, the scattered wolves were not caught, and people bumped into them on the mountain road every now and then.
Ordinary merchants would hire an [Iron-spine Jackal] as a guard when traveling long distances.
The thing was about the same size as a half-sized donkey, with thick skin and thick flesh. A row of iron-gray bristles stood up on its back, like steel needles. It was so fierce that even wild wolves did not dare to get close.
Those who are more particular will bring a [Liaoyuan Monkey] to lead the charge.
Monkeys have good eyesight and can see three or four miles out when squatting at a high place. If there is any disturbance, they will call out in advance so that the master can be prepared.
But that's the pomp of the rich.
A [Iron-spine Jackal] costs 800 coins for a trip to the county town, and with the [Liaoyuan Monkey], it is one or two.
The Luo family can't afford it.
[Chasing the Wind Horse] is the poor man’s choice.
It cannot fight, so it has no choice but to run when it encounters wild beasts.
But it runs fast.
The Level 2 awakened [Wind Chasing Horse] has a natural skill called [Blowing the Wind], which can accelerate with the direction of the wind. When the wind is blowing, it can run more than twice as fast as an ordinary horse.
If it really encounters danger, it can also use the [Quick Charge] skill in a short period of time. Its hooves will fly, and the wind will carry the smoke, and it will jump hundreds of feet away in the blink of an eye.
What cannot outrun it cannot catch up.
Nothing that can catch up with it can be touched in this countryside.
Arrive at the county seat in two quarters of an hour.
Go in and out quickly, leaving no gaps in the road.
The safety of the poor depends on a quick word.
Luo Changgeng asked Luo Chuan to push the wheelbarrow in front of [Chasing the Wind Horse], then stood up slowly while holding on to the edge of the wheelbarrow.
He had a bad back and stood up very slowly, his whole body bowed like an old bow that had been bent.
He raised his head and looked at the [Wind Chasing Horse].
[Wind Chasing Horse] glanced at him with his head tilted, snorted, and scratched his hooves twice impatiently.
Luo Changgeng didn't say hello like a human being.
He bowed seriously towards the horse.
He bent deeply, and the pain in his waist made him grit his teeth, but he didn't say a word.
"Excuse me. This is my boy's first trip back to the county town. Please take care of me on the way..."
He took out a cloth bag from his arms and opened it. Inside was a bunch of copper coins. After counting, there were two hundred copper coins in total. They were tied with hemp rope, no more and no less.
He gently placed the copper coin on the sash pocket on the side of Chai Feng's saddle.
[Chasing the Wind Horse] looked down at the string of copper coins, then at Luo Changgeng, and snorted.
It’s accepted.
Lao Zhao, who was walking on foot, watched this scene with a grass root in his mouth. He didn't say anything, he just tightened the reins of "Chasing the Wind Horse" and nuzzled at Luo Ying.
"Come on, boy. Hold on tight, this beast has a bad temper and will be bumpy at the start."
Luo Ying got on the horse's back.
[Wind Chasing Horse]'s back is much narrower and harder than Lao Hei's, and it hurts his butt bones.
He held the reins with one hand and pressed the horn wrapped in three layers of old cloth in the bookcase beside him with the other hand to confirm that it was still there.
Then he looked back.
Luo Changgeng stood next to the unicycle, holding the handle with one hand and hanging the other hand by his side. The dry tobacco pole was pinned to his waist, and the wind blew his gray temples.
Luo Chuan stood behind his father, with his hands in his belt, his lips pursed tightly, his eyes red, but he did not speak.
Behind them were Zhao Laoliu, Aunt Zhang, Liu Laizi, and a few other folks whose names they couldn't name.
All standing.
They all looked at him.
Luo Ying opened his mouth, wanting to say something.
But when the words came to my mouth, I felt that nothing was right.
title_en: Chapter 4 Carp leaps over the dragon gate
